1	Parashat Bechukotai. The Parashah begins with the words: "If
2	you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments and do
3	them, I will give you your rains in their season, and the land will give its produce,
4	and the tree of the field will yield its fruit. I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down
5	with none to make you afraid, and you will pursue your enemies. Five of you will chase
6	a hundred, and a hundred of you
7	will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword. I will turn to you, make you fruitful,
8	and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you."
9	That is, I will fulfill everything I committed to you.
10	But if you do not walk in My statutes and keep My commandments... This is how
11	the Parashah begins. Rashi writes here: "If you walk in My statutes."
12	Could this be the observance of the mitzvot? What does he mean
13	by "walk in My statutes"? Does he mean here the observance
14	of the mitzvot, when it says "and keep My commandments"? After all,
15	observing the mitzvot is already stated. The Torah doesn't use words for nothing.
16	It says afterward "and keep My commandments." So what is "If
17	you walk in My statutes"? What am I fulfilling with "If you walk in My statutes"?
18	That you be laborious
19	in Torah. That is, the Torah demands of us: be
20	laborious in Torah. Two things. So if you are laborious
21	in Torah, and not only "keep My commandments," but toil in
22	Torah and "keep My commandments," then all the blessings
23	we saw
24	earlier will come. How does toil in Torah enter into the words
25	"walk in My statutes"? After all, the plain meaning of the words implies mitzvot only. Rashi
26	says that otherwise it is redundant. Fine, but how does it imply here
27	that it speaks of Torah? The explanation is
28	this: there are people who treat
29	Torah as if it were just one more thing in life. It's a
30	nice thing sitting there in the library, once in a while you take it and read,
31	but you live as you
32	understand. When a person toils in Torah and enters the
33	deeper layers, not just reading the Torah
34	superficially, not just taking the Torah as one more thing
35	in life, but knowing that the One who created the world
36	created all of creation for the sake of the Torah, so that a person
37	would walk in the ways of the Torah, then he knows that the Torah is
38	a way of life. That is called "walk in My statutes." When can you
39	walk within the statutes, feeling as though you
40	are inside a wonderful system that you swim in
41	like a fish in water? Someone outside the water, carrying
42	a barrel of water on his shoulder, finds it heavy. But when he
43	dives into the water and enters the deep layers, there you go
44	to the coral beach in Eilat, suddenly he begins
45	to discover amazing colorful fish, sees marvelous
46	corals, and he is delighted with pleasure. Whoever is outside knows
47	that when this man was outside, he carried a barrel and it was
48	heavy for him, so he begins to pity him. He might pick up
49	the phone to him: "Aren't you suffocating? You have
50	tons of water on you, enormous atmospheric pressure!" What does he
51	say? The opposite: "What a pleasure it is here! I enjoy it. The more
52	I go deeper, the more I dive, the more I discover
53	new worlds." That is called "walk in My statutes," that you
54	walk within the statutes, not taking it as something
55	external. And how can one reach this? Only through
56	toil in Torah. One who learns Torah with toil, that is,
57	dives into the Torah, not superficially. There are many.
58	Sometimes there are even religious people who grew up religious, then
59	reached age 15, 16, 17, were tempted by all kinds of
60	urges out there, and left. And when you later speak with him about
61	Judaism,
62	he says: "Listen, I've already been there."
63	And he doesn't notice that when he was there, he was very much
64	on the outside. He didn't dive inward. He saw it
65	from outside; his life was mostly run for him as a child. Did he
66	choose what to do? They told him: go to school, now
67	come back, study, open the Chumash, go pray, go
68	put on tefillin, and so on. So they ran his
69	life. When he grew up, he doesn't notice that if he now
70	went in to learn, he would look with a new view. The view
71	would be deeper, more of his own personal choice.
72	And truly there are many who left at a young age and afterward
73	return. Personally, I meet many such people
74	who tell me they started listening to lessons, watching
75	lectures, going to Torah classes. He says: "Never,
76	when I was young, did I know there were such deep layers
77	within the Torah." Why? Because he always
78	knew the Torah externally, as his life was more run
79	for him. And sometimes such people don't feel
80	that their main barrier, at 20, at 30, when he
81	wants to return and feels he has a barrier, and he
82	doesn't always know that his main barrier is
83	precisely that he has in his head "I've already been there." And he
84	doesn't know that this "I was there" is not accurate. You
85	weren't there. You were next to it. You didn't go inside,
86	you didn't dive. Whereas if you had truly entered and dived
87	into the depth of the Torah, you would know the Torah
88	as it truly is, and you would live differently. You would know
89	that the Torah is a way of life, it gives you
90	the right order. After all, what does the Torah really say to a person?
91	Enjoy everything the world has, but I will put your
92	shelves in order: this yes, that no. Meaning,
93	at certain times you are married, you have a wife, but
94	there is family purity. There is work all week, but
95	on the seventh day you shall rest. There are guidelines, there are rules for how
96	to put in order the shelves of everything that touches the
97	functioning of a person in life, for his benefit. But beyond that, the Torah
98	here teaches a person that if you walk in My statutes and
99	keep My
100	commandments, not only do you enter a right
101	and healthy order of life that does you good, with peace of mind, for a soul
102	that walks in the path of truth, there is no happier soul. A person
103	who knows that the truth is on this track and I am walking
104	on that path, what suffering! He knows I am
105	not walking on the right path. But when he knows I am
106	walking on the right path, following the manufacturer's instructions,
107	what happiness, what joy, what satisfaction he has. The soul also
108	feels it is receiving its nourishment. But
109	here the Torah reveals to us another thing: that the moment a person
110	walks on the right path, the Heavenly help that descends
111	to the world is on a completely different level. The Ramchal writes
112	that every action a person does here has a mechanism connecting
113	it to the spiritual worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah.
114	Everything here has a spiritual root
115	above. It acts here, influences above, and the bounty
116	descends to the world, like a rope. Rav Chaim of Volozhin
117	writes a parable of a rope that goes up over a pulley and descends on the other
118	side. When you shake one end of the rope,
119	you cause movement above, and immediately the other end
120	below also begins to move. The same thing: you here
121	act according to the manufacturer's instructions, according to
122	the rules, and immediately influence the upper worlds, and the bounty
123	descends to the world as rains, as peace, as security.
124	In a period when the news reports a shortage of rain,
125	the Kinneret dropping and so on, one of the things we need
126	to do is a personal accounting: where are we in the picture? After all,
127	the Torah connects the state of the rains with the
128	spiritual state of the people of Israel. And we all know what
129	is written: "Happy is one whose toil is in Torah and who gives contentment
130	to his Creator, who grows up with a good name and departs the
131	world with a good name." What does "Happy is one whose toil
132	is in Torah" mean? Every person toils. There is no person who doesn't toil. There is a person
133	who
134	toils in all kinds of vanities, who travels to places where
135	it is forbidden to be, and to see
136	things that are forbidden to see. He toils; it's part of the toil.
137	He might say, "I enjoy it," but he has his toil.
138	There is a person who sits at home idle, bored. That too
139	is called toil. Boredom isn't toil, it is toil
140	of the soul. A person sits bored, staring. What can he
141	do? He too goes through a certain type of toil. Only what
142	is written there is "Happy is one whose toil is in Torah." After all, time
143	passes. Happy are you if you know how to take this time
144	and your toil and lead it according to the Torah, according to
145	the way of the Torah, so that you walk on the right path,
146	the path of truth. May we all merit truly good,
147	happy lives, to overcome all kinds of urges
148	and confusions in the world, and to reach happiness, joy,
149	[Music]
150	and satisfaction.
151	[Music]
